scientific_queries.note: Minimal-evidence experiment on data in hand; no novelty claim.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round's own amendment documents the decision-rule error, and the effect sizes are small enough that no positive claim needs challenging.

design.predictor: cross-cell mean of the other cells; own-data arm adds a 2-parameter affine calibration fitted on m measured pairs
design.metric: precision@10 on the unmeasured remainder; chance 2.9-4.2%

results.saturation: none observed; the 10->25 gain (1.38 pp) exceeds the 0->10 gain (1.19 pp)

decision_rule_error.what: paired(m1,m2) returns precision(m1) - precision(m2); both H050 and H051 were written in the wrong direction
decision_rule_error.consequence: the script's printed verdict 'pooling_is_already_the_ceiling' and flag H051_saturates_by_25 = true are artefacts of the mis-specified rule and are not conclusions
decision_rule_error.corrected: H050 holds (m=10 better by 1.19 pp, CI excludes 0) with a small effect; H051 is refuted (no saturation)

interpretation: cross-cell pooling already reaches 33% precision@10 (11x chance); the target cell's own measurements buy about 1.2 pp per ten and roughly 9 pp at a hundred, so minimal evidence is not small on this design. The calibration model is deliberately weak (two parameters), so this is a statement about weak calibration, not about the uselessness of own data.

register_updates.C18: new, exploratory: pooling precision@10 0.333 (11.3x), own-data gains 1.19 pp at m=10 and 9.20 pp at m=100, no saturation
